newsitem.title: USA: IMF chief shows little concern about currencies.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief shows little concern about currencies.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus delivered an upbeat assessment of the outlook for the world economy on Monday.

In a speech to the IMF's Interim Committee, he evinced little concern about present currency rates, although he said he saw the need for further steps by the United States and Britain to prevent economic overheating.
"Exchange rates among the major currencies are generally consistent with broader policy objectives," the IMF chief said.
The U.S. and Britain have benefitted from the strength of their currencies, which has helped contain inflation.
Camdessus though said he still saw the risk of higher inflation in both countries.

"Several countries that have reached an advanced stage in their current expansion, including the United States and the United Kingdom, are facing risks of overheating and a need for further pre-emptive policy restraint," the IMF chief said.

Echoing the IMF's World Economic Outlook report released last week, Camdessus said the global expansion was likely to continue this year and next. "There are few signs of the tensions and imbalances that usually foreshadow significant downturns," he said.
The outlook has improved in continental Europe and Canada and the recovery in Japan is expected to continue at a moderate pace, Camdessus said.
"Stronger growth during the period ahead should make it easier for the European Union to stick to the timetable for EMU (European monetary union)," he added.
He noted though that both Europe and Japan face what he called "serious structural weaknesses" in their economies that have yet to be satisfactorily addressed.
